Then I just need to gather the computed C rows to rank 0 only when validation or printing is actually requested, since the validation check only touches a small 5x5 corner that's likely already on rank 0 anyway.\n\nI should also handle edge cases like N smaller than the rank count — Gatherv naturally handles zero-count ranks — and N=0 producing NaN or division issues, though I won't over-engineer for that. For timing, I'll wrap the local computation in a barrier, measure elapsed time per rank, then reduce with MAX to get the true wall-clock time of the parallel region, keeping the printed output format essentially unchanged aside from maybe an extra line showing rank count.\n\nSince validation only reads a handful of rows/columns of A and B, I can keep initializing the full matrices on every rank since that cost is trivial compared to the O(N^3) multiply, and only print the \"Initializing matrices...\" message from rank 0 to avoid duplicate output.\n\nFor performance, streaming all of B for every row of C is memory-bound for large N since B can be tens or hundreds of megabytes, so I should block over k and j so a chunk of B stays in cache and gets reused across multiple rows of C, while still accumulating into C in the same k-ascending order to preserve identical floating-point results to the naive version.\n\nI'm register-blocking over 4 rows of C at a time to cut B loads, using restrict pointers to help the compiler vectorize the inner j loop, and sticking to MPI-only parallelism rather than adding OpenMP as a dependency. For load balancing I'll distribute rows in contiguous blocks with remainder handled by the first ranks, gathering results with Gatherv and broadcasting B appropriately.\n\nEach rank can just initialize its own B locally without communication since that cost isn't timed. {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793069300676,"sessionID":"ses_e84bed131ffeFiNTHEjhkThy2X","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01AZiokS7qm8s7fUoH8fD7ZT","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r4/matmul/matmul.cpp","content":"#include <mpi.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Generate pseudo-random values for matrix initialization\nconstexpr double getPseudoRndValue(const size_t N, const size_t i, const size_t j) noexcept {\n    return (((i + 1) * (i + j + 1) * 1299709) % (N * N)) / static_cast<double>(N * N);\n}\n\nvoid initMatrix(std::vector<double>& mat, const size_t N) {\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < N; ++j) {\n            mat[i * N + j] = getPseudoRndValue(N, i, j);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Row-block decomposition of N rows across `size` ranks.\n// The first (N % size) ranks receive one extra row.\nstruct RowRange {\n    size_t begin;\n    size_t count;\n};\n\nRowRange rowRangeFor(const size_t N, const int rank, const int size) noexcept {\n    const size_t r = static_cast<size_t>(rank);\n    const size_t p = static_cast<size_t>(size);\n    const size_t base = N / p;\n    const size_t rem = N % p;\n    return RowRange{r * base + std::min(r, rem), base + (r < rem ? 1 : 0)};\n}\n\n// Computes rows [rowBegin, rowBegin + rowCount) of C = A * B.\n// A and B are full NxN row-major matrices; C is a local rowCount x N row-major buffer.\n//\n// For every C[i][j] the products A[i][k]*B[k][j] are accumulated in strictly\n// ascending k order starting from 0.0, exactly as in the sequential reference,\n// so results are bitwise identical regardless of the number of ranks.\n// Blocking and register reuse only change the order in which different (i, j)\n// elements are visited, never the summation order of an individual element.\nvoid matrixMultiplyRows(const double* A, const double* B, double* C, const size_t N,\n                        const size_t rowBegin, const size_t rowCount) {\n    constexpr size_t BK = 128;  // k-block: B panel of BK x BJ stays cache resident\n    constexpr size_t BJ = 256;  // j-block\n    constexpr size_t RI = 4;    // rows of C processed together (reuses each B load 4x)\n\n    std::fill(C, C + rowCount * N, 0.0);\n\n    for (size_t kk = 0; kk < N; kk += BK) {\n        const size_t kEnd = std::min(kk + BK, N);\n        for (size_t jj = 0; jj < N; jj += BJ) {\n            const size_t jEnd = std::min(jj + BJ, N);\n\n            size_t i = 0;\n            for (; i + RI <= rowCount; i += RI) {\n                const double* a0 = A + (rowBegin + i + 0) * N;\n                const double* a1 = A + (rowBegin + i + 1) * N;\n                const double* a2 = A + (rowBegin + i + 2) * N;\n                const double* a3 = A + (rowBegin + i + 3) * N;\n                double* c0 = C + (i + 0) * N;\n                double* c1 = C + (i + 1) * N;\n                double* c2 = C + (i + 2) * N;\n                double* c3 = C + (i + 3) * N;\n\n                for (size_t k = kk; k < kEnd; ++k) {\n                    const double* b = B + k * N;\n                    const double x0 = a0[k];\n                    const double x1 = a1[k];\n                    const double x2 = a2[k];\n                    const double x3 = a3[k];\n                    for (size_t j = jj; j < jEnd; ++j) {\n                        const double bj = b[j];\n                        c0[j] += x0 * bj;\n                        c1[j] += x1 * bj;\n                        c2[j] += x2 * bj;\n                        c3[j] += x3 * bj;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            for (; i < rowCount; ++i) {\n                const double* a = A + (rowBegin + i) * N;\n                double* c = C + i * N;\n                for (size_t k = kk; k < kEnd; ++k) {\n                    const double* b = B + k * N;\n                    const double x = a[k];\n                    for (size_t j = jj; j < jEnd; ++j) {\n                        c[j] += x * b[j];\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Simple validation: compute a single element and compare\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<double>& A, const std::vector<double>& B,\n                   const std::vector<double>& C, const size_t N) {\n    // Check a few random positions\n    constexpr size_t checkPoints[] = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4};\n    \n    for (size_t pi = 0; pi < 5; ++pi) {\n        for (size_t pj = 0; pj < 5; ++pj) {\n            const size_t i = checkPoints[pi] % N;\n            const size_t j = checkPoints[pj] % N;\n            \n            double expected = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < N; ++k) {\n                expected += A[i * N + k] * B[k * N + j];\n            }\n            \n            const double actual = C[i * N + j];\n            const double relError = std::abs((actual - expected) / (expected + 1e-10));\n            \n            if (relError > 1e-6) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at (%zu, %zu): expected %.10f, got %.10f (error: %.10e)\\n\",\n                       i, j, expected, actual, relError);\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size N (computes NxN * NxN) (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint run(int argc, char** argv, int rank, int size) {\n    const MPI_Comm comm = MPI_COMM_WORLD;\n    const bool root = (rank == 0);\n\n    size_t N = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments (identical on every rank)\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            N = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (root) printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            if (root) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Matrix Multiplication Benchmark\\n\");\n        printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", N, N);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n        printf(\"MPI ranks: %d\\n\", size);\n    }\n\n    // Every rank holds full A and B (deterministic initialization, no communication),\n    // and computes only its own block of rows of C.\n    std::vector<double> A(N * N);\n    std::vector<double> B(N * N);\n    if (root) printf(\"Initializing matrices...\\n\");\n    initMatrix(A, N);\n    initMatrix(B, N);\n\n    const RowRange range = rowRangeFor(N, rank, size);\n    std::vector<double> Clocal(range.count * N);\n\n    if (root) printf(\"Computing matrix multiplication...\\n\");\n\n    // Synchronize so the timed region covers only the parallel computation\n    MPI_Barrier(comm);\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    matrixMultiplyRows(A.data(), B.data(), Clocal.data(), N, range.begin, range.count);\n\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    // Wall time of the parallel region is the slowest rank\n    long long localNs = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();\n    long long maxNs = 0;\n    MPI_Reduce(&localNs, &maxNs, 1, MPI_LONG_LONG, MPI_MAX, 0, comm);\n\n    // Gather full C on rank 0 only when it is needed for output or validation\n    std::vector<double> C;\n    if (printResults || validate) {\n        MPI_Datatype rowType;\n        MPI_Type_contiguous(static_cast<int>(N), MPI_DOUBLE, &rowType);\n        MPI_Type_commit(&rowType);\n\n        std::vector<int> counts, displs;\n        if (root) {\n            C.resize(N * N);\n            counts.resize(size);\n            displs.resize(size);\n            for (int r = 0; r < size; ++r) {\n                const RowRange rr = rowRangeFor(N, r, size);\n                counts[r] = static_cast<int>(rr.count);\n                displs[r] = static_cast<int>(rr.begin);\n            }\n        }\n        MPI_Gatherv(Clocal.data(), static_cast<int>(range.count), rowType,\n                    root ? C.data() : nullptr, root ? counts.data() : nullptr,\n                    root ? displs.data() : nullptr, rowType, 0, comm);\n        MPI_Type_free(&rowType);\n    }\n\n    int status = 0;\n    if (root) {\n        auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(\n            std::chrono::nanoseconds(maxNs));\n\n        printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n\n        // Calculate GFLOPS\n        double gflops = (2.0 * N * N * N) / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n        printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n\n        // Print results for external validation\n        if (printResults) {\n            print_results(C, \"MatrixC\");\n        }\n\n        // Validation\n        if (validate) {\n            printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n            bool valid = validateResult(A, B, C, N);\n\n            if (valid) {\n                printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            } else {\n                printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n                status = 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Make the exit status consistent across all ranks\n    MPI_Bcast(&status, 1, MPI_INT, 0, comm);\n    return status;\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);\n\n    int rank = 0;\n    int size = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &size);\n\n    const int status = run(argc, argv, rank, size);\n\n    MPI_Finalize();\n    return status;\n}\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r4/matmul/matmul.cpp","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r4/matmul/matmul.cpp","time":{"start":1793069300582,"end":1793069300637}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_17b42128a001bQF5DsofB6GJDA","sessionID":"ses_e84bed131ffeFiNTHEjhkThy2X","messageID":"msg_17b41af0a00131rDGjd2NzaJWL"}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793069443742,"sessionID":"ses_e84bed131ffeFiNTHEjhkThy2X","part":{"id":"prt_17b44486c0014T0f4BlSgDB2ab","messageID":"msg_17b44431f001rOstiJ4y7HNDUe","sessionID":"ses_e84bed131ffeFiNTHEjhkThy2X","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm looking at the compiled assembly for the matrix multiply inner loop, noticing GCC used an FMA instruction but also partially vectorized the first couple of k-iterations into separate multiply and add steps, computing the partial sums in order before folding them together.\n\nLooking closer, I realize this is actually non-fused — the vectorized peel does a separate round of multiply then add, unlike the fma elsewhere. So the compiler's floating-point contraction is inconsistent across code paths, applying only where it recognizes the pattern in the scalar loop but not in the vectorized portion. That means matching the original bit-for-bit depends on reproducing the same inconsistent contraction behavior, whereas my version applies fma uniformly everywhere.\n\nSince forcing -ffp-contract=off would eliminate fma entirely and hurt performance, I'd rather keep my uniform fma approach and accept the tiny ~1e-16 relative discrepancy, well within the 1e-6 tolerance — this is normal floating-point evaluation-order variation, not a correctness bug, though I should note it clearly.\n\nChecking the sum/min/max comparisons confirms the relative difference is around 1e-15, which is fine. Now I want to benchmark single-rank and multi-rank performance against the original across varying process counts, so I need to check the core count and set up mpirun with oversubscription if needed before running scaling tests at n=2048.\n\n","time":{"start":1793069434988,"end":1793069443729},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
